title: Rav Ada bar Acha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Zevachim 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.22a.2), from which Hyman infers that he lived in Abaye’s time. In [Keritot 14a](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.14a.13) he said, “Five sin-offerings,” etc. But where he is mentioned in [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.1.2.7), folio 7b, “Rav Hamnuna and Rav Ada bar Acha in the name of Rav,” and likewise in [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.9.3.6), “Rabbi Ba bar Hamnuna, Rav Ada bar Acha in the name of Rav,” Hyman identifies him as Rav Ada bar Ahavah, who is called Achavah or Acha in the Jerusalem Talmud.[^1]

notes.text: The Bavli names Rav Ada bar Acha in the two places; compare [Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=221&lang=en). The consulted Jerusalem Berakhot 1:2 adds Rabbi Idi to the chain and brackets the patronymic אחוא. Guggenheimer’s Gittin 9:3 gives Rabbi Ba bar Hamnuna and Rav Ada bar Acha in the name of Rav. The identification with Ada bar Ahavah remains Hyman’s argument.
